# The GUI grows a right-hand Card view generated by a host-side Card generator

A session's most valuable state is not always prose: what is being worked on, what came out
of the last turn, how far along something is. Today that state exists only as a waterfall of
Assistant messages and Tool cards the reader has to re-read. The GUI gains a right-hand
**Card view** — a small number of model-generated, structured views of the current session —
rendered by json-render in the webview, generated by the Tauri 宿主 as a second, deliberately
narrow provider caller.

Source spec: `.scratch/gui-cards/spec.md`. Terms: **Card view** / **Card** / **Card
generator** / **SpecStream op** (`GLOSSARY.md`).

## Decisions

### D1 — Observer, not a tool

The Card generator fires when a turn **completes**, decided by the host: the main worker's
`stop_reason == Completed` is the trigger. The main agent is never told that Cards exist — no
`render_card` tool, nothing in its system prompt, nothing in its tool set, nothing added to
Message history. Cancelled and failed turns do not trigger (the previous Cards stay), nor do
`new_session` / `resume_session` (a session swap must not silently spend tokens); a manual
`regenerate_cards` command, surfaced as a "generate" control in the panel, is the retry and
debug path.

A tool would make Cards part of the model's workflow: it would cost turn rounds, mutate
Message history, and let the model decide the reader's layout mid-conversation. The Card is a
*derived view* of the session, and derived views belong to the frontend side of the seam.

### D2 — A Card kind is its identity; three kinds, LRU-evicted

The catalog defines a fixed vocabulary of Card kinds — `task-board`, `result`, `insight` — and
the model may only emit SpecStream ops for one of them. The kind is the key: re-generating
`result` replaces that Card rather than appending a fourth, which is what keeps a task board
alive across turns instead of being pushed out by three newer one-shot results. The session
holds at most three Cards, ordered most-recently-updated first; a fourth kind (unreachable
with a closed vocabulary, but reachable after the vocabulary grows) evicts the stalest.

Free-form ids were rejected: a model that spells `task-board` as `task-status` next turn
silently forks the board.

### D3 — Two appliers, one op stream

Every SpecStream op is delivered to the webview **verbatim** and applied there by json-render's
`createSpecStreamCompiler`, one complete line at a time, so the Card grows as the model writes.
Independently, the host applies the same line to a mirror Spec it keeps. Neither applier gates
the other.

The webview applier exists because only it paints; the host applier exists because the host
needs the current Spec without a webview — as the `currentSpec` input of the next generation,
as the snapshot a reloading window receives, and as the unit of LRU eviction and replacement.

Divergence is prevented structurally rather than by discipline: same bytes (the host never
re-serialises an op), same six-operation semantics (the mirror is a tolerant reimplementation
of json-render's `applySpecStreamPatch` — `replace` writes even when the target is absent,
`add` creates missing parents, `remove` of a missing path is silent — **not** a strict RFC 6902
crate), and the same newline framing with the same trailing-partial-line buffer. A test feeds
one op stream to both implementations and asserts the resulting specs are equal.

The host forwards *before* it applies, so a host-side surprise can never withhold a line the
webview would have rendered.

### D4 — Cards ride their own long-lived channel

The per-`prompt` `Channel<GuiWireEvent>` dies with its worker, and Card generation starts when
a turn ends, so it cannot ride that channel. The frontend subscribes once
(`subscribe_cards(channel)`), which **returns the current snapshot** and then streams four flat
events: `card_begin { card_id }`, `card_op { card_id, op }` (the op is one raw JSON string —
the webview's own native input format, never a decomposed object), `card_end { card_id, ok }`,
and `cards_snapshot { cards }`.

A global `emit` + `listen` namespace was rejected: the existing contract is one flat
`kind`-tagged enum per channel, and a second event namespace would have two ways to spell
"something happened in the host".

### D5 — A one-shot call on its own worker, outside the session's accounting

The generator calls `Provider::chat` directly with the two messages, an empty tool list, the
current `ProviderConfig` (`config::load_app_config(settings.overrides())`), its own
`CancelToken`, and a conservative `max_tokens` (4000). It runs on its own thread and is
single-flight; `prompt` cancels it (without joining — a command thread must not block on a
network read) because a new turn instantly makes the old Cards stale, and `dispose` joins it.
It does **not** introduce a `SessionState`: `Running` keeps meaning "the main turn is running".

Its usage is deliberately not folded into `Session.usage`, the Usage HUD or the context
percentage: those answer "what did the conversation cost / how full is the window", and a
display-only side request would corrupt that answer. The cost is invisible in the UI and
recorded only in logs — the accepted trade-off of an automatic generator.

### D6 — Catalog in TypeScript, prompt assembled across the seam

The catalog, its zod props schemas and the component registry are TypeScript (json-render's
own shape). The system prompt is `catalog.prompt()` — generated at runtime in the webview and
sent with each `generate`/`subscribe` request — so there is exactly one description of the
component vocabulary and no build-time codegen whose drift must be policed. The host owns only
the **user** prompt: the session digest, the current Cards as `currentSpec`, and the reason for
this generation. `slimcode-app`'s config resolution means the host needs no new dependency edge
for the provider call.

### D7 — Element-level granularity, frame-batched rendering

Progressive rendering is decided by op granularity, not by the transport. The prompt requires
one element per op and `/root` first, caps a single `Text` payload (~120 characters), and
forbids wrapping a whole Card in one `add` — otherwise the first visible change would arrive
only after the whole card was written. The webview batches ops per animation frame (the same
queue-then-flush pattern the Transcript uses) so a burst of ops is one React render, and
`card_begin` immediately clears the target Card and shows a thin progress bar, so feedback
starts before the first op lands.

Token-by-token text (repeatedly `replace`-ing one `Text`'s content) was rejected: it multiplies
op count and token spend and trains the model to edit text instead of structure.

### D8 — Three components of failure, one place to show them

Bad lines are dropped and good lines kept (models occasionally emit fences or truncate). If no
op applied at all, the previous Card is kept and the panel grows a small retry affordance —
never a transcript block and never the global error banner: a failed side view is not a failed
turn. A single Card whose Spec is structurally wrong degrades through `Renderer`'s per-element
error boundary and `fallback`; the registry supplies a quiet placeholder component for unknown
types so a bad generation leaves a stub, not a hole.

## Considered Options

- **Give the main agent a `render_card` tool** — rejected: Cards become turn-consuming
  modelling work and enter Message history, and the agent starts choosing the reader's layout.
- **Let the model emit the whole Card set as one spec** — rejected: it hands layout authority
  and eviction order to the model, and stalls the visible progression into a single op.
- **Reuse `@json-render/shadcn` (36 Radix components)** — rejected: Radix plus a second visual
  language for a surface that only needs to be read, not filled in. A hand-written ten-component
  catalog in the GUI's existing slate/indigo language is smaller and more predictable.
- **Apply ops only in the webview** (host forwards blindly) — rejected: no `currentSpec` for the
  next generation, no snapshot for a reloading window, nothing to evict.
- **Apply ops only in the host and send finished specs** — rejected: the Card would appear in
  one jump at the end of generation.
- **Persist Cards** (sidecar JSON or a `card` record in the session log) — deferred, not
  rejected: the host already owns the authority, so persistence is additive; v1 keeps them in
  memory, matching the precedent that session cumulative usage is not persisted (ADR-0029 D3).
- **Fold the generator's usage into the HUD** — rejected: the HUD is defined over the session's
  own requests, and a display side-channel would distort it.

## Consequences

- `gui/ui` gains json-render: `@json-render/core` + `@json-render/react` (pinned 0.21.3) and
  `zod@^4` (a peer dependency), plus `cardCatalog.ts` / `cardRegistry.tsx` (the ten components),
  `cards.ts` (the per-Card compiler and the op-to-spec reducer), `CardView.tsx` and its panel
  state; `api.ts` gains `subscribeCards` / `regenerateCards`; `App.tsx` wires the subscription
  and the layout.
- `gui/src-tauri` gains `cards.rs` (tolerant op applier, `CardStore` with the LRU cap, session
  digest builder, the generator worker and its prompt assembly), a `card_sink` slot in the
  controller, and the `subscribe_cards` / `regenerate_cards` commands. The worker-gates
  (`Running` / `Disposed`) and the existing wire enum are unchanged.
- `Cargo.toml` (host) is unchanged: the provider, `ProviderConfig` and config resolution all
  already arrive through `slimcode-app`.
- The CLI, TUI, SDK, FFI and session log formats are untouched — Cards exist only in the GUI
  host's memory, so no other frontend can observe them.
- Cards are lost on session swap and on restart (D2/D8), and the generator's token cost is
  invisible in the UI (D5) — the two boundaries this ADR deliberately accepts.
